title: JSON to XML Converter – Keys to XML Elements | OpenAnyDoc
description: Convert JSON to XML in your browser: objects become elements and arrays repeated elements, ready to copy or download as an .xml file.
heading: JSON to XML Converter
subtitle: Open or paste JSON and its XML appears at once, wrapped in a root element, ready to copy or download; nothing is uploaded.
intro: Need XML for an older SOAP service, an import screen or a feed that will not take JSON? Open, drop or paste your JSON and the XML is shown straight away in a dialog. Each key becomes an element, each array item a repeated element with the same name, and everything sits inside one <root> element so the result is a well-formed document. Copy it or download it as an .xml file; the JSON stays open in the viewer, so you can change it and convert again.

features.title: Private
features.text: Your JSON is converted by your own browser and never sent to a server, so nobody else sees it.

features.title: Well-formed every time
features.text: One <root> element, escaped text and valid element names, so any XML parser can read the result.

features.title: Works offline
features.text: After you have used it once, it keeps working without an internet connection.

stepsTitle: How it works: convert JSON to XML

steps.title: Open or paste your JSON
steps.text: Choose a .json file, drop it on the page, paste it into the box, or try a sample.

steps.title: Read the XML
steps.text: The XML is shown at once in a dialog, indented, with the whole document inside <root>.

steps.title: Copy or download
steps.text: Copy the XML or download it as an .xml file with the JSON file's name.

handles: Objects: each key becomes a child element, in the JSON's order, keys that are whole numbers such as "2024" included.
Arrays: each item becomes a repeated element named after the array's key, so "tags": ["a", "b"] gives two <tags> elements.
null becomes an empty element; numbers and true/false become element text.
Keys that are not valid element names (spaces, a leading digit, symbols) are changed into valid names.
Text with <, > or & is escaped, and Arabic and other non-Latin text is kept as it is.
limits: No attributes are written: every value becomes an element, so XML that needs attributes must be adjusted by hand.
Keys that had to be renamed do not convert back to their original spelling.
faqTitle: JSON to XML: questions and answers

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. The JSON is read and turned into XML by your browser, on your device. Pasted text stays in this tab and is never sent anywhere.

faq.question: Why is everything inside a <root> element?
faq.answer: An XML document must have exactly one top element, while JSON can have several keys at the top or be an array. Wrapping the result in <root> makes it a well-formed document every time.

faq.question: How are JSON arrays written in XML?
faq.answer: XML has no arrays, so each item becomes its own element with the array's key as its name. A list of three users under "user" becomes three <user> elements in a row.

faq.question: What happens to a key like "first name" or "2fa"?
faq.answer: Element names cannot contain spaces or start with a digit, so such keys are changed into valid names. Check the result if a program expects exact names.

faq.question: Can I get attributes instead of elements?
faq.answer: No. The JSON to XML converter writes every value as an element and creates no attributes. That is the limit to plan for if your target format uses attributes.

faq.question: Can I convert XML to JSON as well?
faq.answer: Yes, on the XML to JSON page.

faq.question: How do I convert a JSON file to XML?
faq.answer: Open or paste the JSON in OpenAnyDoc's JSON to XML converter and the XML appears at once, wrapped in one <root> element. Copy it or download it as an .xml file; the JSON is converted in your browser without being uploaded.
